title: Install the fine-tuning tools
description: Installs PyTorch (processor build), Hugging Face Transformers and PEFT for LoRA fine-tuning, plus llama.cpp's converter that turns the trained model into something Ollama can load. All in your home folder, about 2 GB.

uvVersion.description: The uv release used to fetch Python and install packages.

ggufVersion.description: gguf, the file format library llama.cpp's converters use.

llamaCppTag.description: llama.cpp release (2026-09-30) whose converter script and llama-quantize are used.

llamaCppSha256.description: sha256 of llama-<tag>-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz, as GitHub publishes it.

preflight.title: At least 15 GB free in your home folder
preflight.failMessage: Fine-tuning needs room for the tools (about 2 GB), the base model's original weights and checkpoints. Free up space in your home folder first.

preflight.title: Can look up pypi.org and download.pytorch.org
preflight.run: getent hosts pypi.org >/dev/null && getent hosts download.pytorch.org >/dev/null
preflight.failMessage: This machine cannot resolve the Python package servers. Check its internet connection and DNS.

steps.title: Install Python, venv, tmux, git and the OpenMP runtime if they are missing
steps.why: The tools run in their own Python environment; tmux keeps agent sessions alive when your phone disconnects.
steps.skipIf: command -v python3 >/dev/null && python3 -c 'import venv, ensurepip' 2>/dev/null && command -v tmux >/dev/null && command -v git >/dev/null && command -v curl >/dev/null && ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q libgomp.so.1
steps.run:
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 -o Acquire::Retries=3 update -qq
apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 -o Acquire::Retries=3 install -y -qq --no-install-recommends python3 python3-venv tmux git curl ca-certificates libgomp1

steps.title: Install uv (Python package manager) for your user
steps.why: uv installs the tools and the Python version they need into your home folder, without touching the system Python.
steps.skipIf:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$uv" --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q " $P_uvVersion"
steps.run:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
rm -rf "$D/uv"
python3 -m venv "$D/uv"
"$D/uv/bin/pip" install -q --disable-pip-version-check "uv==$P_uvVersion"
"$uv" --version
steps.verify:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$uv" --version >/dev/null

steps.title: Install PyTorch and the training libraries
steps.why: About 2 GB, installed in the background. The processor build of PyTorch is used; it needs no graphics card.
steps.skipIf:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" -c "import torch, transformers, peft, datasets, gguf; assert torch.__version__.split('+')[0] == '$P_torchVersion'" 2>/dev/null
steps.run:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$uv" venv -q --clear --python 3.12 "$D/training/venv"
"$uv" pip install -q --python "$D/training/venv/bin/python" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu "torch==$P_torchVersion"
"$uv" pip install -q --python "$D/training/venv/bin/python" "transformers==$P_transformersVersion" "peft==$P_peftVersion" "datasets==$P_datasetsVersion" "accelerate==$P_accelerateVersion" "gguf==$P_ggufVersion" sentencepiece protobuf safetensors numpy
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" -c "import torch, transformers, peft, datasets, gguf; assert torch.__version__.split('+')[0] == '$P_torchVersion'" 2>/dev/null
steps.verify:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" -c "import torch, transformers, peft, datasets, gguf; assert torch.__version__.split('+')[0] == '$P_torchVersion'" 2>/dev/null
steps.undo:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
rm -rf "$D/training/venv"
steps.facts:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" -c "import torch, transformers, peft; print('training.torch=' + torch.__version__); print('training.transformers=' + transformers.__version__); print('training.peft=' + peft.__version__)"

steps.title: Fetch llama.cpp's converter and quantizer
steps.why: They turn the trained model into a GGUF file of the size you pick, the format Ollama loads. The converter is a Python script; llama-quantize is llama.cpp's own prebuilt processor build, checked against its published sha256. Nothing is compiled.
steps.skipIf:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
[ -f "$D/training/llama.cpp/convert_hf_to_gguf.py" ] && [ -x "$D/training/llama.cpp/bin/llama-quantize" ] && [ "$(cat "$D/training/llama.cpp/.llmwizard-tag" 2>/dev/null)" = "$P_llamaCppTag" ]
steps.run:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
rm -rf "$D/training/llama.cpp"
git -c advice.detachedHead=false clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$P_llamaCppTag" https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp "$D/training/llama.cpp"
mkdir -p "$P_CACHE"
tgz="$P_CACHE/llama-$P_llamaCppTag-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz"
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -C - -o "$tgz" "https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/$P_llamaCppTag/llama-$P_llamaCppTag-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz"
echo "$P_llamaCppSha256  $tgz" | sha256sum -c - || { rm -f "$tgz"; echo "The download does not match its published checksum."; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$D/training/llama.cpp/bin"
tar -xzf "$tgz" -C "$D/training/llama.cpp/bin" --strip-components=1
rm -f "$tgz"
printf "%s" "$P_llamaCppTag" > "$D/training/llama.cpp/.llmwizard-tag"
steps.verify:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" "$D/training/llama.cpp/convert_hf_to_gguf.py" --help >/dev/null && { "$D/training/llama.cpp/bin/llama-quantize" 2>&1 || true; } | grep -qi usage
steps.undo:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
rm -rf "$D/training/llama.cpp"

steps.title: Check that training works on this processor
steps.why: Runs one tiny training step on random numbers, so a broken install shows up now and not hours into a job.
steps.run:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" - <<'PY'
import time, torch
m = torch.nn.Linear(256, 256)
opt = torch.optim.AdamW(m.parameters())
t = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    loss = m(torch.randn(64, 256)).pow(2).mean()
    loss.backward(); opt.step(); opt.zero_grad()
print("ok", torch.__version__, "threads", torch.get_num_threads(), "cpu", torch.backends.cpu.get_cpu_capability(), "%.2fs" % (time.time() - t))
PY
steps.facts:
D="$P_HOME/.local/share/llmwizard"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$P_CACHE/uv" UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$D/python" UV_NO_PROGRESS=1
uv="$D/uv/bin/uv"
"$D/training/venv/bin/python" -c "import torch; print('training.cpuCapability=' + torch.backends.cpu.get_cpu_capability())"
